Multiplication

ArithmeticMental MathCounting
Game: Look for patterns in the table of products of the numbers from 1 to 20.
How to play: Press a number in the table. Its row and column light up, and so does every place the same product appears. Move around with the arrow keys.
Look for the math

The table shows a × b where row a meets column b. Each fact below was checked on the whole 20 by 20 table.

A mirror and a diagonal of squares

Because a × b = b × a, the table reads the same on both sides of the main diagonal, which runs through the squares 1, 4, 9, …, 400. Press any cell off the diagonal: its mirror image lights up. Press a square on the diagonal: only that cell lights, since a square is its own mirror. In fact a product appears an odd number of times only when it is a square.

Rows are counting

Row n goes up in steps of n, so it counts n, 2n, 3n, …. In the nine times table the digits of each answer up to 9 × 10 add to 9: 9, 18, 27, 36, …, 90 give 9 each.

How often does a number appear?

The number p appears once for every way of writing it as a × b with a and b from 1 to 20 (counting a × b and b × a separately). So 12 appears 6 times (1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4 and the mirrors) and 400 appears once. There are only 152 different products in the table, and the most frequent is 60 with 8 places: 3 × 20, 4 × 15, 5 × 12, 6 × 10 and their mirrors. Numbers with many divisors appear most often, and a number such as 17 (a prime) appears only twice, as 1 × 17 and 17 × 1.

Press 24, then 36. Which one is a square? How can you tell from the picture?

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
